description: Shared Renovate preset for every site built on louise-toolkit.

Consume it with { "extends": ["github>bowenlabs/louise-toolkit"] } — that bare form resolves to THIS file (Renovate looks for default.json), and it is fetched from this repo's default branch, so a change here reaches every site on its next run.

Deliberately NOT the same file as this repo's own renovate.json5. That one carries library-specific rules a consuming site has no use for — the create-astroid template ignore, the vite-plus pin. The overlap between the two is intentional and small; a site should not inherit the library's plumbing.
Plain JSON rather than JSON5 because the bare github>owner/repo lookup only checks .json. Reasoning lives in `description` fields instead of comments, which is Renovate's own convention.

packageRules.description: The whole reason a site tracks this preset. Toolkit releases are the updates a Louise site most wants promptly — they carry the editor, auth and content fixes — and they are first-party, so the usual soak-before-trusting-a-stranger argument does not apply. Grouped so a release that bumps two of them lands as one PR, and taken off the weekly schedule so it does not wait until Monday.

Held on 5.x. TypeScript 7.0 is GA but ships without a stable programmatic API until 7.1, and Astro's tooling (@astrojs/check) depends on that API. Lift when 7.1 ships AND @astrojs/check supports it — two conditions, not one.

Only relevant to repos that pin the Vite+ binary in a CI action alongside the devDependency; Renovate can edit only one of the two and would land exactly the skew that check exists to catch. Harmless on a site that does not use it.
Majors get their own PR and a week of soak. The soak is how a broken release gets yanked before it reaches a production site's lockfile.
pnpm itself. These repos install through `corepack pnpm` against the pinned version, and a mismatch surfaces as a store error rather than a clear message. Its own PR so that failure mode is obvious.
Node moves in .nvmrc, engines, and CI together, and on Cloudflare it is a decision about the deploy target rather than a routine bump.
Tooling that cannot reach a visitor. One PR, and the site's own CI is a real test of it.
Patch-level runtime updates, kept apart from the dev group because these actually ship to the edge.
